mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of quarters where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods where UNRATE exceeds 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which lowers earnings expectations for industrial firms and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of episodes where INDPRO declines for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% over two months signals a disinflationary tightening, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises while CPIAUCSL < 2% for two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods where FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls below 2% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real personal income (implied by PAYEMS growth) and a fall in housing starts (HOUST) signals a shift from durable goods investment to services, reducing capital expenditure by S&P 500 constituents and lowering earnings growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth positive while HOUST falls for three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where PAYEMS grows while HOUST declines for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 6% combined with a decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals deepening labor market distress, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 6% and PAYEMS falls for three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods where UNRATE exceeds 6% and PAYEMS declines for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above 4% signals robust aggregate demand, which supports earnings growth and justifies higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where GDPC1 rises by more than 4% year-over-year.
